axis_conversion.unity_dump: original FBX world, left-handed Y-up, scale1
axis_conversion.quaternion_formula: Blender[w,x,y,z] -> Unity[x,y,z,w] = sqrt(0.5)*[x-w,-(y+z),y-z,w+x]; equivalent quaternion signs are normalized for angular error.

findings: Original1H Chop matches across FBX/GLB within floating-point precision at the four requested times.
Original Minion and Warrior GLBs have identical evaluated bone poses for the same three clips at these times.
The supplied Unity1H/Idle world poses match the original FBX after axis/frame conversion; a large pose-direction difference is not present in these56 samples.
1H and2H Chop are different source clips with different trajectories and durations; do not compare them by frame number as if they were the same motion.
limitations: Four sampled times only; not a full animation sweep or a test of every between-key interpolation.
Numeric pose correspondence and source hashes are preservation evidence, not proof of visually finished animation, weapon grip, silhouette, skin deformation or gameplay transitions.
The Unity pose text rounds components to six decimals; the measured sub-micrometre/microradian differences include that output precision.
